made_by.warning: MEASURED, not guessed. The grid was corrected once: the first fit ran 75 ms early and Renjith heard it. Drop 1 confirmed by ear at 63.55 s. Bar phase resolved by the same answer. Chapter boundaries between 63.62 and 107.43 are disputed by six methods and are NOT settled -- see segmentation_proposal, which is recorded and not applied.

grid.how: fitted on the 35-130 Hz band of the ORIGINAL MIX, only in windows where the kick actually plays. On-beat vs off-beat energy ratio reaches 17x.

superseded.why: fitted on full-mix spectral flux across all 128 mel bands, which hi-hats, synths and vocals dominate. 75 ms early. Renjith heard it.

grid.bar_phase_resolved_by: Renjith confirmed the drop by ear. Only bar phase 1 puts that instant on beat 0 of a bar; phase 2 would put it on beat 3, which no dance record does. One human answer settled two unknowns.

moments.note: CONFIRMED by ear. Nearest beat 63.621 s, which is beat 0 of its bar.
measured: the most exposed vocal in the song. Voice 1.00 against drums 0.22. Lands 1.91 s before drop 2 -- voice alone, then the room detonates.
strongest sub-bass step in the song
UNVERIFIED. sub-bass only drop-out, not silence. May not read as a stop at all

vectors.pooling: mean of 75 Hz frames between consecutive beats, then L2-normalised
vectors.note: Beat-aligned pooling makes this tempo-invariant almost for free: 126 bpm and 84 bpm give the same sequence length. Out of line because 369x768 float16 does not belong in JSON. This is the tier for everything nobody has a word for.

energy_note: Composite of on-beat kick strength, sub-band RMS, broadband RMS, high-band RMS and onset density, each normalised on its 3rd-97th percentile. Two features were removed because they INVERT on this record: spectral centroid rises when the bass leaves, so it scored the kick-less intro above the drop; spectral flux measures change rather than level, so a sustained wall of sound read calmer than a sparse verse. Sustained and transient views also disagreed -- 84-92 s has the strongest kick in the song and little sustained low end -- so the composite carries both.

chapters_suspect.why: Energy now ranks the section I labelled 'verse' (16.00-31.24) as the highest in the song at 0.90, above both drops. Either the label is wrong and that is a chorus, or the boundary is. Separately, the stretch I called one continuous 'drop' from 63.62 to 107.43 has a clear energy dip to 0.40 around 84-88 s, which usually means a vocal section sits between two chorus passes and there is a boundary I missed near 78 and 92.

stems.note: Per-instrument presence, normalised 0-1 on the 2nd-98th percentile of each stem. Demucs output ran a uniform +25.08 ms late against the source; corrected once here. This is the field that was missing: a lighting reader wants to spotlight the voice and had no way to know where the voice was.

stem_findings.voice_vacates_both_drops: voice 0.50 -> 0.02 at drop 1, 0.61 -> 0.12 at drop 2, while drums go to 0.99 and 1.00. Vocal out, drums maximum, is the measurable signature of a drop in this song.
stem_findings.hook_is_not_separable: The lead hook stays inside `other`. guitar peaks at 0:12 and piano at 1:11, which are the verse pluck and a chord stab, not the hook. So if we want `the hook plays here` the map needs a field for it -- six-stem separation will not hand it to us.

accents.how: onsets on the lag-corrected Demucs drums stem, prominence>0.055
accents.note: Individual percussive events. NOT beats -- 70.9% of these (697 of 983) do not sit on the beat grid, though only 5.2% miss the 1/16 subdivision, which is the real shape of this drum programming -- and not moments, which are the six structural kinds. A reader that wants to stab three times at second 2 cannot get those times from `beats` or from `stems`, so this field goes in under the rule: a field goes in when a reader breaks without it.

kick_region.measured: drums-stem kick energy steps from 0.383 in bar 9 to 0.949 in bar 10, holds 0.906-0.956 through bar 16, then collapses to 0.143 in bar 17. A 2.5x step in and a 6.7x drop out, both on the bar he named.
kick_region.note: Not stored as a new field: `stems.drums` already carries it and no reader breaks without a declaration. Recorded as verification of the measured curve.

three_hits_at_2s.note: the three most prominent drum onsets between 1.5 and 3.0 s; a pickup into bar 2 at 2.663

observations.note: The observation tier. Everything measured, additive and append-only -- unlike the interface tier (beats, downbeats, chapters, moments, spans, energy) which readers compile against and which stays deliberately small. Be miserly with promises, generous with observations.

chords.how: chroma template match over bass+other+guitar+piano, 36 templates (maj, min, dom7), median-smoothed across 3 bars

bass_notes.how: autocorrelation f0 on the 38-420 Hz band of the bass stem

stereo.note: Everything before this pass decoded to mono, which threw the width away. A left-right rig maps onto pan directly.

melody.how: autocorrelation f0, 80-800 Hz, 55 ms window, unvoiced=null

microtiming.unit: ms from the nearest 1/16 of a beat
microtiming.corrected: The first version measured deviation from the nearest BEAT and reported an IQR of +/-115 ms, which is half a beat -- an artifact of assigning subdivision hits to beats, not a measurement of feel. Feel is deviation from the grid the music is actually played on.

brightness.note: Texture, not level. `It gets brighter` is not `it gets louder`, and a filter sweep is the signature EDM gesture -- previously invisible.

notes.how: Spotify basic-pitch (ICASSP 2022) via the ONNX backend, polyphonic, per stem, onset 0.55 / frame 0.35 / min 70 ms, lag-corrected by 25.08 ms
notes.note: I had said polyphonic transcription was hard and not close to free. It is a pip install. The tflite backend failed on a NumPy 2.x ABI break -- the exact trap written into listen/GPU.md -- so this uses ONNX, which is numpy-2 clean.

lyrics.how: Whisper small, word timestamps, on the Demucs vocals stem, lag-corrected. Words come from the isolated voice, so the timings are not confused by the mix.
lyrics.note: Syllable timing is what lets a show sing along, and it is the one fact no other listener supplies. Also the decisive test of any recalled timeline: a language model can quote the lyrics of this song from memory, but only the audio says WHEN they land.
lyrics.caveat: Whisper's WORDS are unreliable on a sung, separated stem -- it heard 'What's up on a young year' for 'Once upon a younger year'. Its TIMES are good. So use it for timing and get the words elsewhere: the better architecture is forced alignment of the real lyrics against the audio -- recall for the words, measurement for the times.

vocal_silence.how: gaps of 1.5 s or more between Whisper word timings on the vocals stem, snapped to downbeats
vocal_silence.note: The cleanest structural evidence in the song. A 35.7 s instrumental window spans the whole of drop 1, and a 14.9 s one begins exactly at drop 2 -- a third independent confirmation that the voice vacates both drops.

sections.note: Which sections are the SAME section. Two chapters both called `drop` were previously indistinguishable, so a reader could not make the second one bigger than the first -- and escalating a repeat is most of what makes a show feel written for one song rather than driven by a features. `id` groups them by measured similarity of stem presence, energy and chord content; `repeat` counts occurrences; `arc` is position in the song.
sections.how: cosine similarity of a 19-dim per-chapter centroid, greedy clustering at 0.955

segmentation_proposal.by: MERT-v1-95M beat vectors, checkerboard novelty at a 16-beat scale, snapped to downbeats
segmentation_proposal.why: Five methods now say my chapters are wrong between 63.62 and 107.43: the energy dip at 84-88, the vocal returning at 78.86, a 35.7 s instrumental window, my own clustering refusing to merge the two drops, and now the learned space scoring drop E against drop G at 0.951 -- the same section. The learned space also pairs the two breaks at 0.95, which my named clustering also split, and pairs my 'verse' with a drop at 0.94, which is the sixth signal that the 16.00-31.24 label is wrong.
segmentation_proposal.status: PROPOSAL, not applied. Renjith's ear is the authority on structure and he is at bar 16 of 92. Recorded so it is one keypress to accept rather than an argument to have.
